title: From Ethiopian Goats to Global Cafes: How Coffee Spread Across the World
title_zh: 从埃塞俄比亚的山羊到全球咖啡馆：咖啡如何传遍世界
intro_zh: 本文约 573 词，围绕咖啡如何从埃塞俄比亚传遍世界展开，包含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Coffee is one of the world's most popular drinks. Yet its journey began in Ethiopia, East Africa. An old legend tells of Kaldi, a goat herder. He saw that his goats became lively after eating red berries from a tree. Kaldi tried the berries and felt full of energy. Coffee plants grew wild there. People first chewed the berries or mixed them with fat. Later, they made a drink from roasted seeds.
paragraphs.zh: 咖啡是世界上最受欢迎的饮品之一。然而，它的旅程始于东非的埃塞俄比亚。一个古老的传说讲述了牧羊人卡尔迪的故事。他看到自己的山羊在吃了某种树上的红色浆果后变得活跃起来。卡尔迪尝了那些浆果，感觉充满能量。咖啡树确实在那里野生生长。人们最初咀嚼浆果，或将它们与脂肪混合。后来，他们用烘焙过的种子制作饮品。

paragraphs.en: By the 15th century, coffee had crossed the Red Sea to Yemen. The port city of Mocha became famous for shipping coffee. Yemeni farmers planted trees and guarded them closely. They sold only roasted beans, not live plants, to control the trade. From Aden, merchants loaded coffee onto ships. The beans traveled to Mecca, Cairo, and Istanbul. Coffee was no longer local; it was a valuable product.
paragraphs.zh: 到15世纪，咖啡已越过红海到达也门。港口城市摩卡因运输咖啡而闻名。也门农民种植咖啡树并严密看守。他们只出售烘焙过的豆子，而不卖活植株，以控制贸易。在亚丁，商人将咖啡装上船。咖啡豆运往麦加、开罗和伊斯坦布尔。咖啡不再只是地方饮品，而是一种有价值的产品。

paragraphs.en: In the Arab world, coffee found a home in monastery and prayer halls. Sufi Muslims drank it to stay awake during long night prayers. Soon, public coffee houses appeared in Mecca and Istanbul. People gathered to drink coffee, listen to music, play chess, and discuss news. Some leaders feared these crowded shops might encourage political talk. Sometimes they closed them. Still, the drink grew more popular.
paragraphs.zh: 在阿拉伯世界，咖啡在修道院和祈祷厅找到了归宿。苏菲派穆斯林饮用它，以便在漫长的夜间祈祷中保持清醒。很快，公共咖啡馆出现在麦加和伊斯坦布尔。人们聚集在那里喝咖啡、听音乐、下棋、讨论新闻。一些领导人担心这些拥挤的店铺可能鼓励政治讨论。有时他们关闭了这些店铺。尽管如此，这种饮品还是越来越受欢迎。

paragraphs.en: Coffee reached Europe in the early 17th century. Venetian traders brought it from the Ottoman empire. Some Europeans called it the 'bitter invention of Satan' and asked the Pope to ban it. One story says Pope Clement VIII tasted coffee and liked it so much that he blessed it. Coffee soon spread through Italy, France, and England. London's first coffee house opened in 1652. By 1700, the city had more than 2,000.
paragraphs.zh: 咖啡在17世纪初到达欧洲。威尼斯商人从奥斯曼帝国带来咖啡。一些欧洲人称它为“撒旦的苦涩发明”，并要求教皇禁止它。一个故事说，教皇克莱门特八世品尝咖啡后非常喜欢，于是赐福于它。咖啡很快传遍意大利、法国和英国。伦敦的第一家咖啡馆于1652年开业。到1700年，该市已有2000多家。

paragraphs.en: European powers wanted their own coffee supplies. The Dutch were among the first to succeed. They introduced coffee plants to Java, in present-day Indonesia, in the late 17th century. The climate was perfect. Dutch growers shipped coffee to Amsterdam, and from there it was exported across Europe. The French planted coffee in Martinique, in the Caribbean. The Spanish took it to Central and South America. Coffee became a global crop, but its spread also brought slave labor on plantations.
paragraphs.zh: 欧洲列强想要自己的咖啡供应。荷兰人是最早成功的国家之一。他们在17世纪晚期将咖啡树引入今印度尼西亚的爪哇。那里的气候非常理想。荷兰种植者将咖啡运往阿姆斯特丹，再从那里出口到整个欧洲。法国人在加勒比海的马提尼克岛种植咖啡。西班牙人将其带到中美洲和南美洲。咖啡成为一种全球作物，但它的传播也带来了种植园中的奴隶劳动。

paragraphs.en: Brazil became the world's largest coffee producer. Coffee arrived there in the early 18th century. A story says a Brazilian officer charmed a French governor's wife and received a few coffee seeds hidden in a bouquet. True or not, Brazil's huge land and suitable climate let coffee farming expand quickly. By the 1830s, coffee was Brazil's main export. Today, Brazil still produces about one third of the world's coffee.
paragraphs.zh: 巴西成为世界上最大的咖啡生产国。咖啡在18世纪初到达那里。一个故事说，一位巴西军官迷住了法国总督的妻子，并收到几粒藏在花束中的咖啡种子。无论真假，巴西广阔的土地和适宜的气候使咖啡种植迅速扩展。到19世纪30年代，咖啡成为巴西的主要出口产品。今天，巴西仍生产世界约三分之一的咖啡。

paragraphs.en: In the 20th century, coffee became an everyday drink. Instant coffee, invented in the early 1900s, made a cup quick and cheap. After World War II, coffee chains opened in many countries. Italian-style espresso and cappuccino won fans worldwide. In the 1970s and 1980s, large American companies began selling coffee in comfortable cafes. They turned coffee drinking into a social experience. Today, people enjoy coffee in many ways, from Turkish coffee to cold brew.
paragraphs.zh: 20世纪，咖啡成为一种日常饮品。20世纪初发明的速溶咖啡使一杯咖啡变得快捷便宜。二战后，咖啡连锁店在许多国家开业。意式浓缩咖啡和卡布奇诺赢得了全世界的粉丝。在20世纪70年代和80年代，美国大公司开始在舒适的咖啡馆里卖咖啡。他们把喝咖啡变成一种社交体验。今天，人们以多种方式享用咖啡，从土耳其咖啡到冷萃咖啡。

paragraphs.en: Coffee also reflects local cultures. In Ethiopia, a coffee ceremony can last for hours. Green beans are roasted and brewed in front of guests. In Italy, many people drink a quick espresso while standing at a bar. In Turkey, coffee is often served with a glass of water and a piece of sweet candy. These traditions show that coffee carries history and identity. When you drink a cup, you taste a story that crossed oceans and mountains.
paragraphs.zh: 咖啡也反映当地文化。在埃塞俄比亚，咖啡仪式可以持续数小时。绿咖啡豆在客人面前烘焙和冲泡。在意大利，许多人站在酒吧里快速喝一杯浓缩咖啡。在土耳其，咖啡通常配一杯水和一块甜糖。这些传统表明，咖啡承载着历史和身份认同。当你喝下一杯时，你品尝的是一个跨越海洋和山脉的故事。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Coffee is only popular in Europe and America.
Coffee spread from Ethiopia to the rest of the world over centuries.
Coffee was first discovered by Dutch traders.
Coffee houses were banned in all countries.
questions.explain: 文章按时间顺序讲述咖啡从埃塞俄比亚起源，经也门、阿拉伯世界、欧洲、美洲到全球的传播历程，因此主旨是 B。

questions.q: According to the passage, why did Yemeni farmers sell only roasted beans?
options: To keep the coffee plants a secret and control the trade.
questions.explain: 第二段提到也门农民只卖烘焙豆、不卖活植株，是为了控制贸易，故选 A。

questions.q: What can be inferred about coffee houses in London by 1700?
options: They were all closed by the government.
They were mainly used for religious prayers.
They had become common places for social and business activities.
They sold only tea and chocolate.
questions.explain: 第四段说伦敦 1652 年出现第一家咖啡馆，到 1700 年超过 2000 家，并成为商业、科学和闲谈的非正式中心，可推断它们已成为常见的社交与商业场所。

questions.q: The word 'exported' in Paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: sent goods to other countries for sale
questions.explain: export 意为出口，把商品运往他国销售；文中说咖啡从阿姆斯特丹被 exported across Europe，故选 B。
